5-6: A percentage of a quantity: the part as a number.
What percentage one amount is of another.
A percentage of the marbles in a bag after more are added.
Percentages of guests that make up all but a few: the number of guests.
Two changes by a percentage one after the other, up and then down or two discounts: the result against one change.
A price after a discount: the price before it.
A percentage of a percentage: the part of the whole.
One amount more than another by a percentage: by what percentage the other is less.
A percentage that changes after some are taken away: the amount at the start.
A percentage of a group that must come out a whole number: how big the group can be.
Water in fresh and in dried fruit or grass as percentages: the part that is not water stays the same, so the weight after drying comes from it.
One amount raised and another lowered by percentages come out equal, such as one up by 20 per cent and the other down by 20: how the two compared at first.
A share known only to lie strictly between two percentages: the smallest group in which a whole number of members gives such a share.
A total made of several people's parts, each share found from how much the total grows when that part alone doubles: the shares add up to the whole, so the last one is what is left.
Buses counted as crowded above some number of passengers: the share of passengers riding in crowded buses is at least the share of buses that are crowded.
Three amounts linked by percentages, the middle one so much more than the first and so much less than the last: by what percentage the last is more than the first.
Two sides of a rectangle, each changed by a percentage: by what percentage its area changes, which is not the sum of the two changes.
A tank so many per cent empty holds a known amount more than when it is so many per cent full: that amount is 100 per cent less both percentages of the tank, which gives its size.
A tank filled at a steady rate, how full it is given as a percentage at two times: how full it was at the start, by the same percentage gained every hour.
Offers such as one at half price for each one bought, or three for the price of two: compared by what one item costs on average, as a percentage off.
